objective: Choose a monotonic PV inverter Volt-VAR curve that mitigates low-voltage sag and high-voltage swell over a short feeder time series without exceeding inverter reactive-power capability.

submission_schema.volt_var_curve: List of points with strictly increasing voltage_pu and monotonic non-increasing q_fraction in [-1, 1]. Positive q_fraction injects reactive power; negative absorbs reactive power.

hard_constraints: Volt-VAR curve voltage_pu breakpoints must be strictly increasing.
Volt-VAR curve q_fraction values must be monotonic non-increasing as voltage rises.
Reactive power command at each timestep must stay within inverter capability sqrt(kVA^2 - kW^2).
Corrected voltage at each timestep must remain within voltage_limits_pu.

metrics.name: feasible
metrics.description: Whether the curve is monotonic, respects inverter Q limits, and clears all voltage-limit violations.

metrics.name: voltage_violation_timesteps
metrics.description: Time steps whose corrected voltage remains outside the allowed band.

metrics.name: control_effort_kvar_sum
metrics.description: Sum of absolute reactive-power commands over the public time series.

metrics.name: score
metrics.description: Normalized [0,1] score: 1 minus a small scaled reactive-control-effort penalty if feasible, else 0.

source_provenance.title: Local reactive-power control by distributed PV generators
source_provenance.notes: Primary PV reactive-power-control sources; the task selects a Volt-VAR curve under capability and voltage constraints.
